did_you_know.text: Did you know? The queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles, accompanied by a large caravan of camels carrying spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones.

Did you know? The queen of Sheba was impressed not only by Solomon’s wisdom, but also by the food at his table, the organization of his court, the clothing of his servants, his cupbearers, and the ascent by which he went up to the house of the Lord.
Did you know? The queen of Sheba said that she had not believed the reports about Solomon until she came herself; then she discovered that she had not even been told half of his wisdom.
Did you know? The queen of Sheba connected Solomon’s greatness with the Lord’s rule over Israel: she blessed the Lord for appointing Solomon king to administer justice and righteousness.
Did you know? The queen of Sheba gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones; the text emphasizes that there had never been spices like those she brought.
Did you know? Hiram’s servants and Solomon’s servants, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
Did you know? The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents, besides the gold brought by merchants and traders, and by all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land.
Did you know? Solomon’s throne is described as an ivory throne overlaid with gold, with lions standing on each side and on the six steps; the text says that no kingdom had ever made anything like it.
Did you know? Solomon’s ships, which operated with Hiram’s servants, arrived once every three years, carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
Did you know? Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years. After his death, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Rehoboam succeeded him as king.
